subject: Reserved commit: term, staggered start, and SLA credit proposal
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@starlabs.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved commit: term discussion and start schedule

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation, I put together two packaging options for Starlabs' production workload so the team can evaluate tradeoffs between term length and unit pricing:

Option A — 24‑month reserved commit (recommended)
- GPU pool: 48x A100 equivalent (pooled across regions)
- Throughput target: 750 rps sustained 95th pct for 8k context
- Onramp: 60% capacity live day 1, 100% by month 4
- Discount: 34% off list hosted rate (volume amortized over term)
- SLA credits: standard SLA; additional 6% monthly credit for misses > 3 incidents

Option B — 36‑month reserved commit (larger discount, longer lock)
- GPU pool: 48x A100 equivalent (same sizing)
- Throughput: same SLOs
- Onramp: 40% day 1, 70% month 3, 100% month 8 (staggered to align with ML rollout)
- Discount: 42% off list
- SLA credits: standard SLA; 10% monthly credit for misses > 3 incidents in a quarter

We can also do a 12‑month pilot commitment (smaller pool, higher price) if you prefer to shorten procurement cycles.

I've attached the term sheet and a quick MAAP (model allocation and anticipated peaks) workbook so you can validate the sizing assumptions. Two items we need your input on to finalize pricing:
1) Firm target start date for committed capacity (do you want e.g., Jan 1 or Feb 1 2028?)
2) Confirmation of acceptable onramp cadence (we can frontload capacity if you need burst windows).

If Procurement prefers a blended monthly invoice schedule, we can show amortized cashflow and the impact to unit economics.

Quick ask: can you share who from procurement should receive the term sheet? I will follow up with a version that has explicit invoice milestones.

Thanks —
Monica

--
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555‑0192

From: Lena Ortiz <lena@starlabs.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@starlabs.ai>, Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@marco.diaz@starlabs.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved commit: term discussion and start schedule

Monica —

Appreciate the clear options. A few clarifying questions from procurement and infra:

- Can you break the discount into (a) committed unit discount and (b) commitment length credit? Procurement wants to show CFO an annualized savings table.
- For the SLA credit language: how do you define an "incident" for the 95th pct SLO? We need to map to our internal monitoring.
- Onramp windows: Starlabs' model rollout likely spikes in month 2 (internal ML experiments). Is there an option to include a short-term burst pool that does not count against the committed baseline for months 2–3?

Procurement contact: procurement@starlabs.ai (they asked for the term sheet PDF and a high-level cost schedule). Can you send a version with line‑item monthly cashflow for both options?

Thanks,
Lena

--
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering, Starlabs AI
lena@starlabs.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2027 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Reserved commit: term discussion and start schedule

Rishi/Karthik —

Looping you in to answer the procurement questions and confirm the burst pool language. Key asks from Starlabs: monthly cashflow for each option, clearer SLA incident definition, and an option to add a short burst pool for the initial experiment months that wouldn’t reduce their baseline committed capacity.

My proposals:
1) Break discount into two line items in the term sheet: committed unit price (list minus X%) + term-length credit (one-time credit amortized monthly). That makes the CFO table neat.
2) SLA incident: tie to token‑level latency > SLO for > 5 minutes for a single region, or > 0.5% of requests exceeding latency SLO within a rolling 1‑hour window. Need legal to review but this is operationally measurable.
3) Burst pool: We can offer a 10% burst buffer for months 2–3 for free (non-billable) if they accept a 36‑month term; otherwise, for 24‑month term we can offer burst at cost (no additional discount). We should quantify the dollar exposure.

Can you please draft the two cashflow schedules and a short SLA definition paragraph I can send back to Lena? Attachments: redwood-dedicated-term-sheet-v3.pdf (will update with split discounts)

-Monica

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 27 Oct 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved commit: term discussion and start schedule

Monica —

Drafts attached (see workbook pivot tabs). Short notes:
- Pricing approach: commit price per GPU‑hour = list * (1 - commit_discount). Term_credit = flat $/GPU‑hr amortized monthly; includes additional 8% effective discount for 36 months vs 24 depending on start gating.
- Burst pool: if we do free 10% burst for months 2–3 under 36 months, exposure capped at ~ $45k over the two months assuming 10% peak utilization; I recommend including a clause that if burst sustained beyond 45 days we recalculate baseline (protects us).
- SLA definition: propose "incident" = any region where rolling 1‑hour P95 token latency > target for >= 5 minutes OR error rate > 0.5% for >= 5 minutes. Credits tied to monthly billing (0–10% scale based on severity/recurrence).

I also flagged the billing team about amortized vs upfront invoicing — procurement may ask for monthly invoicing with a deposit escrow.

—Rishi

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@starlabs.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@starlabs.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Reserved commit: term discussion and start schedule

Hi Lena / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick turn. Per your asks, attached are: (1) a clean term sheet with the discount split and the amortized monthly schedules for Option A (24m) and Option B (36m), and (2) a short SLA appendix with an operational incident definition and the credit table. See the highlights below:

- 24‑month (Option A): 34% base discount; term credit amortized = $0.018/GPU‑hr; monthly invoice option OK with 20% upfront deposit. Onramp: 60% day 1 -> 100% by month 4.
- 36‑month (Option B): 42% base discount; term credit amortized = $0.030/GPU‑hr; includes a complimentary 10% burst buffer for months 2–3 (exposure capped at $45k). Onramp: 40% day 1 -> 70% month 3 -> 100% month 8.
- SLA: "Incident" defined as rolling 1‑hour P95 latency > target for >= 5 minutes OR error rate > 0.5% for >=5 minutes. Credits scale 2%–10% of monthly committed spend based on frequency and severity. Clause: sustained burst > 45 days triggers baseline recalculation.

Next steps: 1) Procurement, please confirm if you want monthly invoicing vs. quarterly. 2) If Starlabs signs the 36‑month, we’ll include the burst buffer language in Section 4 and remove the deposit requirement. 3) If you prefer a different start date than Jan 1 2028, tell us the target and we’ll rebuild timelines and invoice milestones.

Attaching: redwood-dedicated-term-sheet-v3.pdf, SL-4872-MAAP.xlsx

Happy to hop on a 30‑minute call this week to walk through the cashflow table.

Best,
Monica

--
